faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Short and clear — how we work and what you get

q1.a: Payment is split into milestones: a deposit to start the project and the remaining balance when the website is ready to launch. Payment method can be discussed — bank transfer or other convenient options.

q2.a: On average: Starter — up to 2 weeks, Growth — 3–4 weeks, Premium — 4–6 weeks. Timelines depend on pages, languages and automation scope.

q3.q: What is included in revision rounds?
q3.a: A revision round is a consolidated list of changes you send as one batch. We implement it and present an updated version. The number of rounds depends on your package.

q4.q: Will I be able to edit content myself?
q4.a: Yes. Growth and Premium include a CMS so you can edit texts and pages on your own. We provide onboarding and documentation.

q5.q: How do the CRM and leads from the site work?
q5.a: Leads from the website and WhatsApp are automatically sent to your CRM (Notion, Airtable, HubSpot, etc.). You see clients, statuses and request history in one place.

q6.q: Who pays for CRM, CMS and automation services?
q6.a: Licenses and subscriptions for CRM, CMS, chatbot platforms, WhatsApp Business API and other external services are paid by the client. I help you choose, set up and integrate the right tools.

q7.q: Do you integrate WhatsApp and chatbots?
q7.a: Yes. WhatsApp integration is possible in every package. In Starter — basic lead capture. In Growth and Premium — flows, lead qualification and chatbots, including AI when needed.

q8.a: Yes. Growth and Premium include multilingual support (typically RU / EN / HE). Starter can add it as an option.

q9.q: Who pays for hosting and domain?
q9.a: Hosting, domain and third-party platforms are paid by the client directly. I help you choose the best option and configure everything end-to-end.

q10.q: Can we start small and expand later?
q10.a: Yes. Many clients start with Starter or Growth and later add CRM, automation or new pages. The project is built with scalability in mind.

q11.q: What if I need custom logic?
q11.a: If your needs go beyond the package, we discuss the solution and cost upfront. No hidden work or surprise fees.

clientStories.name: Yael Cohen
clientStories.story: We’re a small tech business and kept postponing a website refresh. The old site was built years ago and stopped helping with sales.
clientStories.challenge: The site looked outdated, didn’t explain what we do, and didn’t generate inquiries. Most clients reached out directly or came from referrals.
clientStories.solution: We got a clear website with a strong structure, services-first messaging, and simple WhatsApp contact. The process was calm and straightforward.
clientStories.quote: The website finally became a working tool, not just a business card. It’s easier to explain what we do and handle requests.

clientStories.name: David Levi
clientStories.story: We’re an offline business with loyal clients, but we knew we were losing new orders without a proper website.
clientStories.challenge: We wanted a clean, modern website — without overloaded design or complex systems.
clientStories.solution: We built the site around collections, examples, and fast WhatsApp contact. No extra features — just clear logic.
clientStories.quote: No miracles promised — just a clean website that genuinely helps our business.

clientStories.story: We work in healthcare, so trust and clear explanation are critical.
clientStories.challenge: It’s hard to explain technical and medical processes in simple terms. Clients kept asking the same questions.

clientStories.quote: Now the website truly supports sales conversations. Clients come more prepared.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: We are committed to making this website accessible to the widest possible audience, including people with disabilities and users of assistive technologies. We continue to improve the accessibility of the website and its interfaces in line with applicable requirements and reasonable technical capabilities.

commitment.title: Our accessibility approach
commitment.text: We treat accessibility as an important part of digital product quality and user experience.
items: we aim to design pages, navigation, and forms so they are convenient for different users
accessibility is considered when developing new pages, components, and updates
we continue addressing identified barriers as the website evolves

standard.title: Standards and references
standard.text: The website is built with reference to accessibility expectations applicable to digital services in Israel and to widely accepted international web accessibility guidance.
items: WCAG AA principles are taken into account during design and development
page and interface structure is created with semantics and predictable behavior in mind
we aim for compatibility with modern assistive technologies

features.title: What is already being implemented
features.text: The website uses practices that help improve interaction for keyboard users, screen reader users, and visual readability.
items: logical heading and section structure
labels and aria attributes for important interactive elements
visible focus states for keyboard navigation
attention to text readability and contrast
clear wording for buttons, links, and forms

compatibility.title: Compatibility
compatibility.text: The website is designed to work in modern browsers, on mobile devices, and with basic assistive technologies.
items: responsive presentation across desktop, tablet, and mobile
the interface is intended to remain usable during keyboard navigation
we aim to support screen readers in common browsing scenarios

content.title: Content, documents, and media
content.text: We try to publish content in a way that is easier to understand and navigate, although some items may still require further adaptation.
items: images and visual blocks are accompanied by meaningful text alternatives where reasonably possible
new pages are checked for baseline accessibility before publication
if the website includes documents or embedded third-party materials, their accessibility may depend on the original source

limitations.title: Known limitations
limitations.text: Despite our efforts, some parts of the website may not yet be fully optimized for every accessibility scenario.
items: some animations, decorative effects, or third-party integrations may require additional adaptation
some older parts of the website may be improved gradually rather than all at once
if you encounter a barrier, we would appreciate your feedback

feedback.title: Accessibility feedback
feedback.text: If you notice an accessibility issue, you may let us know. This helps us identify and remove real barriers more quickly.
items: describe the page or feature where the problem occurred
if possible, include the device, browser, and interaction method used
we will try to review the report and find a reasonable solution

contact.title: How to contact us
contact.text: For accessibility-related questions about the website, you may use the contact details shown on the website. It is helpful to include the subject of your request and a short description of the issue.
items: specify the page where the issue occurred
describe what was inaccessible or difficult to use
where appropriate, we may offer an alternative way to receive the information

clinic.title: Clinic Booking Demo
clinic.description: Online doctor booking with CRM lead delivery and inquiry tracking.

caseStudy.challenge: In clinics, leads often get lost: calls, WhatsApp, and forms all end up in different places. A clear and fast booking flow was needed without putting extra pressure on staff.
caseStudy.solution: We created a demo booking platform where the patient selects a service and time slot, and the request is automatically sent to the CRM. The administrator sees all inquiries and statuses in one place.
results: Booking without calls and chaotic messaging

legal.title: Real Estate Legal Services Demo
legal.description: Premium landing page for legal support in real estate transactions in Israel.

caseStudy.challenge: Property buyers, especially foreign investors, often do not fully understand the legal risks of a transaction. Law firms need a clear digital channel to explain risks, demonstrate expertise, and attract high-budget clients.
caseStudy.solution: We developed a premium landing page for a law firm specializing in real estate transactions in Israel. The site explains key legal risks, demonstrates legal expertise, and invites users to book a consultation. It includes multilingual support (EN / HE / RU), a legal fee calculator, and a convenient consultation form.
results: Clear presentation of legal risks for investors
Focused on high-budget real estate transactions
Optimized for lead generation and consultations

musicteacher.title: MusicTeacher4You
musicteacher.description: A platform for finding teachers, booking lessons, and communicating online.

caseStudy.challenge: The task was to unite students and teachers in one system: search, scheduling, booking, and communication — without spreadsheets or manual coordination.
caseStudy.solution: We designed a product with user roles, filters, slot calendars, booking, built-in chat, and video calls. The focus was on a clear UX and a strong mobile experience.
results: Transparent history of lessons and bookings

hm.title: HM Production
hm.description: Service showcase website for photo, video, web, and design with a trust-first approach.

caseStudy.challenge: The goal was to present the studio’s services without overload: style, work examples, and a quick way to get in touch — without lengthy explanations.
caseStudy.solution: We built a concise website with a strong visual presentation, clear service structure, and portfolio focus. The goal was a strong first impression and a simple CTA.
results: Portfolio as the main trust driver
